title: Floor-standing and wall-mounted media units
intro: Floor-standing and wall-hung media units may look similar but transfer loads differently. Distinguish cabinet support from screen support and prepare the substrate, connection and service review.
goals: Separate cabinet and screen support paths
Document the substrate and connection chain

sections.title: Separate cabinet and screen support paths
sections.text: A floor-standing unit transfers weight through base or legs to the floor and may need anti-tip restraint according to its system and use. A wall-hung unit transfers through carcass joints to suspension and wall. A screen may sit on the unit or use a separate mount: draw its path independently and never assume decorative cladding support is adequate for the screen.
sections.caption: Bearing, restraint and screen support are distinct functions.

sections.title: Document the substrate and connection chain
sections.text: Visible finish does not identify the supporting substrate. Obtain wall construction, condition and concealed-service information from the site. Trace carcass, carcass connection, suspension member, substrate fixing and supporting material, assigning review responsibility. A qualified party must select fixing type, number, dimensions and locations for the actual system, substrate and loads; the schematic is not drilling guidance.
sections.caption: Each link needs identification and a review reference.

sections.title: Review access and approval sequence
sections.text: Draw tool access and removal routes for cabinet and screen without damaging finishes; keep service points reachable. Establish hold points for site information, system/load review, component inspection before concealment and qualified installation inspection. Record evidence, owners and open items. A level front or smooth door action alone does not establish suspension adequacy.
sections.caption: Inspect concealed connections before closure and preserve service access.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The proposal hangs a cabinet on timber cladding with no information about the wall behind it. Hold approval until the substrate, carcass, suspension and screen-support path are reviewed. A floor-standing alternative may be studied, but its stability and restraint still need review; changing type does not remove verification.
example.decision: Decision: hold suspension approval until the support chain is documented and reviewed.

quiz.question: Can a level cabinet front justify suspension approval without substrate data?
options: No; complete support data and review
quiz.explanation: Alignment does not establish the adequacy of the support chain.

assignment.prompt: Submit floor-standing/wall-hung alternatives, screen load paths, substrate data, connection chain and approval/access plan.
criteria: Owners and evidence at hold points

faq.question: Does floor support remove the need to review restraint?
faq.answer: No. Review restraint needs for the system and use in addition to vertical bearing.
